newsitem.title: USA: NOMO LEADS DODGERS PAST CARDINALS.
newsitem.headline: NOMO LEADS DODGERS PAST CARDINALS.

text.p: Hideo Nomo allowed two hits over eight innings and Eric Karros belted a two-run homer as the Los Angeles Dodgers took sole possession of first-place in the National League West with a 4-1 win over the St. Louis Cardinals Thursday.
Nomo (15-10), who no-hit the Cardinals for the first 5-1/3 innings, allowed a solo homer to Ron Gant with one out in the sixth and Dmitri Young's eighth inning pinch-hit single.

At Colorado, Ellis Burks had four hits and five RBI and became the 11th player in National League history with 30 homers and 30 stolen bases in a season as the Colorado Rockies completed a three-game sweep of the Atlanta Braves with a 16-8 victory.
Burks singled twice, doubled and hit his 37th homer and joined the 30-30 club when he stole his 30th base in the bottom of the eighth inning.
"It was very exciting. My goal was to stay healthy this year. I worked hard in the off-season and it paid off," he said.
In Houston, Darryl Kile pitched a seven-hitter and Jeff Bagwell and Derek Bell each drove in a pair of runs to give the Houston Astros a 4-1 victory over the Philadelphia Phillies.
Houston won for just the fourth time in its last 11 games.
Kile (12-8) went the distance for the fourth time this season and first since July 5th at Atlanta. He did not walk a batter and struck out nine.
In Montreal, Henry Rodriguez hit a two-run homer with two out in the bottom of the eighth inning to give the Montreal Expos their sixth straight home win, 5-4 over the Florida Marlins.
Dave Veres (5-3) pitched a hitless eighth for the win and Mel Rojas worked the ninth for his 30th save.
In San Francisco, Al Martin drew a bases-loaded walk to snap a tie as the Pittsburgh Pirates scored five times in the sixth inning to defeat the San Francisco Giants 10-4.
Jason Schmidt (4-5) allowed four runs and eight hits over five innings for his first win since June 25th when he was with the Atlanta Braves.
